newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-RYDER CUP SELECTION REMAINS UNALTERED.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RYDER CUP SELECTION REMAINS UNALTERED.

text.p: European captain Severiano Ballesteros suffered a major blow on Tuesday in his bid to retain the Ryder Cup at Valderrama in September when his calls to change the selection process were turned down.
The tournament committee of the PGA European Tour and the Ryder Cup committee jointly announced that, after taking legal advice, the selection process would not be altered.
That means that the top 10 players in the Ryder Cup points list will automatically qualify and Ballesteros, like his predecessors, will have just the two wild card selections.
Ballesteros, along with several leading European players, had called for four selections rather than two.
"Valderrama is a tough golf course and demands special players," he said.
"I don't care what the Americans do in terms of the rules, I only care about having the strongest team."
The Ryder Cup committee took legal advice after hearing that a number of players were also opposed to the change in the rules.

"After taking legal advice, with a view to holding a ballot on the selection procedure, we must end all speculation as leading counsel has made it crystal clear that any change in the procedure could be legally challenged by any one player," said Neil Coles, chairman of the PGA European Tour board of directors and a member of the Ryder Cup committee.
Coles said Ballesteros would be invited to attend future meetings to debate the issue in readiness for the 1999 tournament.
